67:     private val live: Boolean = context?.isLive() ?: true
68:     private val closed = AtomicBoolean(false)
69:     private val generation = AtomicLong(0)
70: 
71:     private val pages = object : LinkedHashMap<Int, List<T>>(16, 0.75f, true) {
72:         override fun removeEldestEntry(eldest: MutableMap.MutableEntry<Int, List<T>>): Boolean =
73:             size > MAX_PAGES
74:     }
75:     private val inFlight = HashSet<Int>()
76:     private var lastFirst = -1
77:     private var lastLast = -1
78:     /** Whether a page has reported an exact total (offset source) vs a growing count. */
79:     private var knownTotal = false
80: 
81:     private val totalSignal: WritableSignal<Int> = Signals.signal(0)
82:     private val loadingSignal: WritableSignal<Boolean> = Signals.signal(true)
83:     private val errorSignal: WritableSignal<Throwable?> = Signals.signal(null)
84:     private val hasMoreSignal: WritableSignal<Boolean> = Signals.signal(true)
85:     private val versionSignal: WritableSignal<Int> = Signals.signal(0)
86: 
87:     /** The full item count (0 until the first page reports it). */
88:     val total: Signal<Int> get() = totalSignal
89: 
90:     /** Whether the initial page is still loading. */
91:     val loading: Signal<Boolean> get() = loadingSignal
92: 
93:     /** The last page failure, or null. */
94:     val error: Signal<Throwable?> get() = errorSignal
95: 
96:     /** Whether more pages exist (cursor/unknown-total sources). */
97:     val hasMore: Signal<Boolean> get() = hasMoreSignal
98: 
99:     /** Changes when a page arrives or is evicted; read by the paged `ForEach`. */
100:     internal val version: Signal<Int> get() = versionSignal
101: 
102:     init {
103:         context?.onClose { close() }
104:         if (live) {
105:             // Start the count/first page before the lazy window is known; the
106:             // engine's prefetch then loads the window's remaining pages.
107:             ensureLoaded(0, pageSize - 1)
108:         }
109:     }
110: 
111:     /** Ensure the pages covering the absolute item range `[first, last]` load. */
112:     fun ensureLoaded(first: Int, last: Int) {
113:         if (closed.get() || !live) {
114:             return
115:         }
116:         val safeFirst = first.coerceAtLeast(0)
117:         val safeLast = last.coerceAtLeast(safeFirst)
118:         lastFirst = safeFirst
119:         lastLast = safeLast
120:         val firstPage = safeFirst / pageSize
121:         val total = totalSignal.get()
122:         val lastPage = when {
123:             // Discover the count from the first page before loading the rest.
124:             !knownTotal && total <= 0 -> firstPage
125:             // Unknown/cursor total: the count grows as pages arrive; do not cap.
126:             !knownTotal -> safeLast / pageSize
127:             else -> minOf(safeLast / pageSize, (total - 1) / pageSize)
128:         }
129:         if (lastPage < firstPage) {
130:             return
131:         }
132:         for (page in firstPage..lastPage) {
133:             loadPage(page)
134:         }
135:     }
136: 
137:     /** The loaded item at [index], or null when its page is not loaded. */
138:     fun row(index: Int): T? {
139:         if (index < 0) {
140:             return null
141:         }
142:         val page = pages[index / pageSize] ?: return null
143:         return page.getOrNull(index % pageSize)
144:     }
145: 
146:     /** Drop the cache and reload the last requested window. */
147:     fun refresh() {
148:         if (closed.get()) {
149:             return
150:         }
151:         generation.incrementAndGet()
152:         pages.clear()
153:         inFlight.clear()
154:         knownTotal = false
155:         loadingSignal.set(true)
156:         errorSignal.set(null)
157:         versionSignal.set(versionSignal.get() + 1)
158:         if (lastFirst >= 0) {
159:             ensureLoaded(lastFirst, lastLast)
160:         }
161:     }
162: 
163:     override fun close() {
164:         if (!closed.compareAndSet(false, true)) {
165:             return
166:         }
167:         generation.incrementAndGet()
168:         pages.clear()
169:         inFlight.clear()
170:     }
171: 
172:     private fun loadPage(page: Int) {
173:         if (pages.containsKey(page) || !inFlight.add(page)) {
174:             return
175:         }
176:         val token = generation.get()
177:         val offset = page * pageSize
178:         val stage: CompletionStage<Page<T>> = try {
179:             val async = asyncLoader
180:             if (async != null) {
181:                 async.load(offset, pageSize)
182:             } else {
183:                 val blocking = checkNotNull(blockingLoader)
184:                 CompletableFuture.supplyAsync({ blocking.load(offset, pageSize) }, executor)
185:             }
186:         } catch (failure: Throwable) {
187:             applyError(token, page, failure)
188:             return
189:         }
190:         stage.whenComplete { value, failure ->
191:             if (failure != null) {
192:                 applyError(token, page, failure)
193:             } else {
194:                 applyPage(token, page, value)
195:             }
196:         }
197:     }
198: 
199:     private fun applyPage(token: Long, page: Int, value: Page<T>?) {
200:         apply(token, page) {
201:             val result = value ?: Page(emptyList())
202:             pages[page] = result.items
203:             val loadedEnd = page * pageSize + result.items.size
204:             knownTotal = result.total != null
205:             val nextTotal = result.total ?: maxOf(totalSignal.get(), loadedEnd)
206:             totalSignal.set(nextTotal)
207:             hasMoreSignal.set(
208:                 result.hasMore || (result.total != null && nextTotal > loadedEnd),
209:             )
210:             loadingSignal.set(false)
211:             errorSignal.set(null)
212:             versionSignal.set(versionSignal.get() + 1)
213:         }
214:     }
215: 
216:     private fun applyError(token: Long, page: Int, failure: Throwable) {
217:         apply(token, page) {
218:             loadingSignal.set(false)
219:             errorSignal.set(failure)
220:         }
221:     }
222: 
223:     private fun apply(token: Long, page: Int, block: () -> Unit) {
224:         if (closed.get() || token != generation.get()) {
225:             return
226:         }
227:         val current = context
228:         if (current != null) {
229:             current.submit(
230:                 Runnable {
231:                     if (!closed.get() && token == generation.get()) {
232:                         inFlight.remove(page)
233:                         block()
234:                     }
235:                 },
236:             )
237:         } else {
238:             inFlight.remove(page)
239:             block()
240:         }
241:     }
242: 
243:     companion object {
244:         private const val MAX_PAGES = 20
245: 
246:         /** A blocking page loader; runs on [executor]. */
247:         @JvmStatic
248:         fun <T> ofBlocking(
249:             pageSize: Int,
250:             loader: PageLoader<T>,
251:             executor: Executor = DataExecutors.SHARED_IO,
252:         ): PagedDataSource<T> = PagedDataSource(pageSize, loader, null, executor)
253: 
254:         /** A `CompletionStage` page loader. */
255:         @JvmStatic
256:         fun <T> ofAsync(pageSize: Int, loader: AsyncPageLoader<T>): PagedDataSource<T> =
257:             PagedDataSource(pageSize, null, loader, DataExecutors.SHARED_IO)
258:     }
259: }

7: /**
8:  * Routes raw input events into the app's bindings via a `RenderResult`'s maps.
9:  *
10:  * One `dispatch(Event)` call handles every event type (pointer, text, value,
11:  * date, media, fit, visible range, navigation); unknown targets are ignored.
12:  */
13: class InputDispatcher(
14:     result: RenderResult,
15:     private val activePath: WritableSignal<String>,
16: ) {
17:     private val tapActions = result.tapActions
18:     private val navigateActions = result.navigateActions
19:     private val textInputs = result.textInputs
20:     private val valueInputs = result.valueInputs
21:     private val editingInputs = result.editingInputs
22:     private val dateInputs = result.dateInputs
23:     private val mediaInputs = result.mediaInputs
24:     private val fitInputs = result.fitInputs
25:     private val visibleRanges = result.visibleRanges
26:     private val navigateHandler = result.navigateHandler
27: 
28:     /** Dispatch every event in a decoded batch. */
29:     fun dispatch(events: Iterable<Event>) {
30:         for (event in events) dispatch(event)
31:     }
32: 
33:     /** Route a single raw input event into the app's bindings. */
34:     fun dispatch(event: Event) {
35:         when {
36:             event.isPointerUp -> {
37:                 val nav = navigateActions[event.target()]
38:                 if (nav != null) nav.run()
39:                 else tapActions[event.target()]?.run()
40:             }
41:             event.isTextChanged -> textInputs[event.target()]?.accept(event.text()!!)
42:             event.isValueChanged -> valueInputs[event.target()]?.accept(event.value())
43:             event.isEditingChanged -> editingInputs[event.target()]?.accept(event.b() != 0)
44:             event.isDateChanged -> dateInputs[event.target()]?.accept(event.days(), event.millisOfDay())
45:             event.isMediaPlayStateChanged -> mediaInputs[event.target()]?.onPlayStateChanged(event.mediaPlaying())
46:             event.isMediaTimeUpdated -> mediaInputs[event.target()]?.onTimeUpdated(event.mediaValue())
47:             event.isMediaEnded -> mediaInputs[event.target()]?.onEnded()
48:             event.isMediaVolumeChanged -> mediaInputs[event.target()]?.onVolumeChanged(event.mediaValue())
49:             event.isMediaDurationChanged -> mediaInputs[event.target()]?.onDurationChanged(event.mediaValue())
50:             event.isFitChanged -> fitInputs[event.target()]?.accept(event.fitIndex())
51:             event.isVisibleRange -> visibleRanges[event.target()]?.onVisibleRange(
52:                 event.visibleFirstIndex(),
53:                 event.visibleCount(),
54:             )
55:             event.isNavigate -> {
56:                 if (event.url() != null) {
57:                     activePath.set(event.url()!!)
58:                 } else {
59:                     navigateHandler?.accept(event)
60:                 }
61:             }
62:         }
63:     }
64: }

1: # ADR-0016: Framework-neutral async and paged data sources for lists
2: 
3: **Status:** Proposed
4: **Recorded:** 2026-11-16
5: **Scope:** Authoring/runtime data sources, lazy-window prefetch, session lifecycle, SSR
6: **Supersedes:** None (extends ADR-0014/ADR-0015 for external data)
7: 
8: ## Context
9: 
10: Applications commonly render lists from a database or a REST API. Today
11: `ForEach` accepts only a `List<T>` or a `Signal<List<T>>`, and the lazy window
12: needs a finite item count plus random access. Wiring a database or REST list
13: therefore requires the application to fetch, materialize, marshal to the
14: session actor, and refresh manually — repeated for every list and framework.
15: 
16: The runtime already provides the necessary pieces:
17: 
18: - a per-session actor and `SessionContext.submit` for external results,
19: - topic subscriptions (`PathlandSignalHub`) for invalidation,
20: - a lazy window that reports the visible range and can prefetch,
21: - a per-session root factory (`PathlandApp.newRoot`) built inside the session
22:   context.
23: 
24: ## Decision
25: 
26: Provide framework-neutral data sources in the JVM library, with optional
27: adapters:
28: 
29: - **`AsyncDataSource<T>`** for small lists: loads all items once, exposes
30:   `items`/`loading`/`error`, and supports `refresh`/`close`.
31: - **`PagedDataSource<T>`** for large lists: offset/limit and cursor/hasMore
32:   pages, a bounded page cache, `total`/`loading`/`error`, and
33:   `ensureLoaded(first, last)` driven by the lazy window.
34: - **Async API:** blocking loaders and `CompletionStage` loaders in the core; an
35:   optional Kotlin coroutines adapter module. No coroutines, Mutiny, or Spring
36:   dependency in the core.
37: - **`ForEach(source)`** for paged sources: loaded items render normally,
38:   unloaded rows render a placeholder of the same main-axis extent.
39: - **SSR loading state:** data sources start in the loading state; the SSR HTML
40:   renders the application's loading/skeleton view. The SSR session does not run
41:   async page loads (it is discarded); the live session loads and sends deltas.
42:   Applications may opt into a synchronous preload later.
43: - **Session lifecycle:** data sources capture the session context, apply results
44:   on the actor, detect SSR vs live (`isLive`), and close via `onClose`.
45: - **Rust:** a `pathland-view-data` std crate provides the same concepts for the
46:   desktop hosts, using the existing `VisibleWindow`/`ForEach` window handle.
47: 
48: Exact requirements live in `spec/DSL.md` §Virtualized lists,
49: `spec/LAYOUT.md` §Virtual extent, and `docs/data-sources.md`.
50: 
51: ## Rationale
52: 
53: - The application should describe *what* data a list shows, not the async,
54:   paging, placeholder, and lifecycle plumbing for each list.
55: - A blocking + `CompletionStage` core works for JDBC/JPA (blocking) and REST
56:   clients (`CompletionStage`/`Uni`) from both Java and Kotlin hosts without a
57:   new core dependency.
58: - The session actor already provides the single-threaded signal contract;
59:   applying external results through `submit` keeps renderers and effects
60:   unchanged.
61: - SSR cannot await arbitrary async work after the session closes; a loading
62:   state is honest and lets the live session fill the data.
63: - Offset/limit is simple and supports random access/counts; cursor/keyset is
64:   more performant and stable for large or append-only feeds. Supporting both
65:   lets the application choose per data source.
66: - A placeholder row preserves the virtual extent and scrollbar while pages
67:   load, so the list never collapses.
68: 
69: ## Alternatives
70: 
71: - **Require applications to materialize a `Signal<List<T>>` manually.** Rejected
72:   as the primary path: it repeats paging/placeholder/SSR/lifecycle code in every
73:   app and has no window-driven prefetch.
74: - **A Kotlin-only `suspend`/`Flow` core API.** Rejected: the library is used by
75:   Java hosts and the Quarkus extension; coroutines remain an optional adapter.
76: - **A Mutiny/Reactor-specific core.** Rejected: framework coupling; adapters
77:   belong at the edges.
78: - **SSR blocking preload as the default.** Rejected: an arbitrary REST/DB call
79:   would block the SSR request; the loading state is the default and preload is
80:   opt-in.
81: - **A generic infinite-stream abstraction without a count.** Rejected for v1:
82:   the protocol's `ITEM_COUNT` and the lazy window need a finite, addressable
83:   range; cursor sources grow the count as pages arrive.
84: 
85: ## Consequences
86: 
87: - `ForEach` gains a data-source overload; the lazy stack/grid call
88:   `prefetch(first, last)` on the initial and adaptive windows.
89: - `SessionContext` gains `isLive()` and `onClose(Runnable)`; the server session
90:   runs cleanup callbacks on close.
91: - The core gains a small `dev.pathland.view.data` package; an optional
92:   `pathland-view-data-coroutines` module adds `suspend` loaders.
93: - The Quarkus demo gains an in-memory `TrackRepository`; the MusicPlayer library
94:   uses a paged source. Docs show Panache/JDBC/REST examples.
95: - SSR renders a loading state; applications that need SSR data can opt into a
96:   preload.
97: - The protocol is unchanged.
98: 
99: ## Sources and current contract
100: 
101: - Lazy window: [LAYOUT.md §Virtual extent](../../spec/LAYOUT.md#virtual-extent-lazy-containers).
102: - Authoring rules: [DSL.md §Virtualized lists](../../spec/DSL.md#virtualized-lists-lazyvstack--lazyhstack).
103: - External updates: [docs/external-updates.md](../external-updates.md).
104: - Related decisions: [ADR-0014](0014-virtualized-lazy-stacks.md),
105:   [ADR-0015](0015-reactive-lazy-prefetch.md).

1: # Data sources (databases, REST APIs)
2: 
3: Pathland lists are usually backed by a database or a REST API. The JVM library
4: provides framework-neutral data sources so an application supplies a loader and
5: the runtime handles async loading, session-actor application, loading/error
6: state, and (for large lists) paging and placeholders.
7: 
8: Decision record: [ADR-0016](./decisions/0016-async-paged-data-sources.md).
9: 
10: ## Status
11: 
12: | Piece | Status |
13: |---|---|
14: | `AsyncDataSource<T>` (load-all) | Implemented |
15: | Kotlin coroutines adapter (`pathland-view-data-coroutines`) | Implemented |
16: | `PagedDataSource<T>` (offset/limit) + `ForEach(source)` | Implemented |
17: | Cursor/`hasMore` pages | Planned (Phase 3) |
18: | Invalidation via topics | Planned (Phase 4) |
19: | Rust `pathland-view-data` crate | Planned (Phase 5) |
20: 
21: ## Async API
22: 
23: The core accepts a **blocking loader** or a **`CompletionStage` loader**:
24: 
25: ```kotlin
26: fun interface ListLoader<T> { fun load(): List<T> }
27: fun interface AsyncListLoader<T> { fun load(): CompletionStage<List<T>> }
28: ```
29: 
30: Why this shape:
31: 
32: - Java and Kotlin hosts can both use it.
33: - JDBC/JPA are blocking; the data source runs the loader on an executor.
34: - Quarkus REST Client/Mutiny and Spring `WebClient` expose `CompletionStage`;
35:   adapt with `uni.asCompletionStage()` / `Mono.toFuture()`.
36: - No coroutines, Mutiny, or Spring dependency in the core.
37: - Kotlin apps can use the optional coroutines adapter.
38: 
39: ## Load-all: `AsyncDataSource<T>`
40: 
41: Use it for small lists (dropdowns, headers, “recently played”, a few hundred
42: rows).
43: 
44: ```kotlin
45: class RecentTracksView(private val repo: TrackRepository) : Component() {
46:     private val recent = AsyncDataSource.ofBlocking { repo.recentTracks() }
47: 
48:     override fun body(): View = VStack {
49:         when {
50:             recent.loading.get() -> Text("Loading…")
51:             recent.error.get() != null -> Text("Could not load recent tracks")
52:             else -> ForEach(recent.items) { track, _ -> TrackRow(track) }
53:         }
54:     }
55: }
56: ```
57: 
58: The data source exposes:
59: 
60: - `items: Signal<List<T>>`
61: - `loading: Signal<Boolean>`
62: - `error: Signal<Throwable?>`
63: - `refresh()` — reload, ignoring stale results
64: - `close()` — ignore in-flight results (also registered on session close)
65: 
66: `ForEach(items)` is the existing list overload; no engine change is needed.
67: 
68: ### Async loader
69: 
70: ```kotlin
71: val tracks = AsyncDataSource.ofAsync {
72:     restClient.tracks().toCompletableFuture() // or Uni.asCompletionStage()
73: }
74: ```
75: 
76: ### Coroutines adapter
77: 
78: Add `dev.pathland:pathland-view-data-coroutines` and use a `suspend` loader:
79: 
80: ```kotlin
81: val tracks = AsyncDataSource.fromSuspend(scope) { repo.recentTracksSuspend() }
82: ```
83: 
84: The adapter bridges through `CompletionStage`; the core stays coroutine-free.
85: 
86: ## Session and SSR behavior
87: 
88: - The data source captures `SessionContext.current()` when constructed (the root
89:   view is built inside the session context).
90: - **Live session:** loading starts immediately; results are applied on the
91:   session actor via `submit`.
92: - **SSR session:** loading starts in the **loading state** and no async load is
93:   run; the SSR HTML renders the application's loading/skeleton view. The live
94:   session loads the data and sends the delta after hydration.
95: - `SessionContext.isLive()` distinguishes the two; `SessionContext.onClose(...)`
96:   closes data sources with the session.
97: - Applications that need SSR data can call a synchronous preload explicitly
98:   (planned); the default is the loading state.
99: 
100: ## Paged lists: `PagedDataSource<T>`
101: 
102: For large lists, a paged source drives the lazy window:
103: 
104: ```kotlin
105: val tracks = PagedDataSource.ofBlocking(
106:     pageSize = 50,
107:     loader = { offset, limit -> repo.page(offset, limit) }, // Page<Track>
108: )
109: 
110: LazyVStack {
111:     ForEach(tracks, itemExtent = 64f, placeholder = { SkeletonRow() }) { track, _ ->
112:         TrackRow(track)
113:     }
114: }
115: ```
116: 
117: Implemented behavior:
118: 
119: - `Page<T>(items, total, hasMore, nextCursor)`.
120: - Offset/limit pages with a bounded page cache (20 pages) and in-flight dedupe.
121: - The lazy stack calls `prefetch(first, last)` for the initial and adaptive
122:   windows; pages load ahead of the viewport.
123: - Unloaded rows render the placeholder at the same main-axis extent; the
124:   virtual extent and scrollbar stay correct.
125: - `total` is exact for offset sources; an unknown total grows as pages arrive
126:   (cursor/`hasMore` sources; the cursor mode itself is Phase 3).
127: - `refresh()` drops the cache and reloads the last requested window.
128: - A live session loads pages asynchronously; SSR starts in the loading state.
129: - `itemExtent` is required for paged sources (the full list is not known).
130: 
131: The MusicPlayer demo's `LibraryView` uses a paged source over the in-memory
132: `MediaPlayerService` (a 40 ms simulated latency, 50-row pages); unit-test
133: mounts without a session context use the in-memory list for determinism.
134: 
135: The coroutines adapter adds `PagedDataSource.fromSuspend(scope, pageSize) { … }`.
136: 
137: ## Quarkus examples
138: 
139: - **In-memory repository (the demo):** `MediaPlayerService.page(offset, limit)`
140:   returns a `Page`; the `LibraryView` wraps it in a `PagedDataSource`.
141: - **Panache:** `query.page(offset / pageSize, pageSize).list()` plus
142:   `query.count()`; map to `Page`.
143: - **JDBC:** `limit ? offset ?` plus a count query.
144: - **REST Client (Mutiny):** return `Uni<PageResponse>` and adapt with
145:   `asCompletionStage()`.
146: - **Executor:** pass a Quarkus managed executor to the data source; results are
147:   still applied on the session actor.
148: 
149: ## Rust (planned)
150: 
151: A `pathland-view-data` std crate will mirror the concepts for desktop hosts:
152: `Page<T>`, `PagedDataSource<T>`, and a `PagedList<T>` that implements
153: `View`/`LazySource`, using the existing `VisibleWindow`/`ForEach` window handle.

(End of file - total 153 lines)

1: # Architecture decision records
2: 
3: ADRs explain **why** Pathland makes consequential architectural choices.
4: [`spec/`](../../spec/) defines the **current contract**; each implementing
5: project's `status.md` tracks **implementation coverage**. ADRs do not introduce
6: additional mandatory behavior or replace either source of truth.
7:

11: |-----|----------|--------|

13: | [0002](0002-native-declarative-layout.md) | Declarative structure and native renderer-owned layout | Accepted |
14: | [0003](0003-application-state-and-delta-emission.md) | Application-owned state and diff-based emission | Accepted |
15: | [0004](0004-binary-input-events.md) | Binary input events rather than payload callbacks | Accepted |

20: | [0009](0009-cross-language-conformance.md) | Language-owned bindings checked by shared conformance data | Accepted |
21: | [0010](0010-server-side-proxy-composition.md) | Server-side composition through ordinary protocol sessions | Accepted |

27: | [0016](0016-async-paged-data-sources.md) | Framework-neutral async and paged data sources for lists | Proposed |

29: ## Conventions
30: 
31: Source-reference syntax, review obligations, drift resolution, and validation
32: commands are defined in [Architecture traceability and drift](traceability.md).
33: The [Pathland architecture skills](skills.md) provide reusable orientation,
34: decision-authoring, review, and maintenance workflows for these conventions.
35: 
36: - Use `NNNN-short-decision-name.md`, allocated sequentially. Never reuse a
37:   published number. Resolve provisional number collisions before merging.
38: - Start with [the template](template.md). Keep context, decision, rationale,
39:   alternatives, consequences, and source links distinct.
40: - Status is **Proposed**, **Accepted**, **Rejected**, or **Superseded**. A
41:   proposal is not binding; only a maintainer can accept a new decision.
42: - Accepted records preserve decision history. Correct factual errors in place;
43:   change a decision through a new ADR and mark the old one Superseded, linking
44:   both records. Update the index and current specs in the same change.
45: - Link ADRs to the relevant specs, and specs back to the ADRs. Keep complete
46:   requirements in specs so readers need not follow rationale links to find them.
47: - `AGENTS.md` retains essential guardrails and points here for rationale.
48:   READMEs retain orientation and usage instructions.
49: - Do not invent alternatives, benchmarks, author approval, or recovered intent.
50:   Identify uncertainty explicitly; an uncertain new proposal stays Proposed.
51: 
52: ## Initial extraction provenance
53: 
54: ADRs 0001–0013 were extracted on **2026-11-12** from existing specifications,
55: READMEs, and `AGENTS.md`. Their Accepted status records decisions already
56: expressed by those sources; it does not claim a new approval or an original
57: decision date. Each record links its evidence. Consequences describe implications
58: of the documented choice, not a reconstructed historical evaluation.

511: #### Virtualized lists (`LazyVStack` / `LazyHStack`)
512: 
513: A `LazyVStack`/`LazyHStack` containing a `ForEach` is a **windowed data
514: container**. The app supplies the collection and the row builder; the engine
515: owns the window and evaluates the builder only for visible rows:
516: 
517: ```kotlin
518: LazyVStack(spacing = 0) {
519:     ForEach(items) { item, _ ->
520:         RowView(item)
521:             .frame(height = 44f)   // fixed main-axis extent
522:     }
523: }
524: ```
525: 
526: Rules:
527: 
528: - `ForEach` inside a lazy stack is a **data source**, not an eager child list.
529:   Outside a lazy stack it keeps its eager behavior.
530: - The lazy stack's content MUST be exactly one `ForEach` for virtualization;
531:   other children keep the eager stack behavior.
532: - `ITEM_COUNT` = the collection size. `ITEM_EXTENT` = the row's fixed main-axis
533:   size, read from the first realized row's `HEIGHT` (VStack) / `WIDTH` (HStack).
534:   If the row has no fixed main-axis frame, the author MUST pass an explicit
535:   `itemExtent` (e.g. `ForEach(items, itemExtent = 44f)`); otherwise the DSL
536:   reports an authoring error. Every row MUST use the same extent.
537: - Variable heights: `ForEach(items, itemExtents = listOf(44f, 60f, …))`
538:   (Rust: `ForEach::item_extents(vec![…])`) supplies one main-axis extent per
539:   item. The engine emits `ITEM_EXTENTS` for the window, `FIRST_ITEM_OFFSET`, and
540:   `TOTAL_EXTENT`; `ITEM_EXTENT` remains the default estimate for items outside
541:   the window. Lazy grids use a uniform extent.
542: - `FIRST_ITEM_INDEX` = the window start. The engine sets it; the author does not.
543: - The DSL sets `EVENT_LISTENERS` bit 10 (`VISIBLE_RANGE`) and routes the event
544:   to the engine's internal window; the author does not manage a window signal.
545: - The engine may prefetch a bounded, directional margin around the visible
546:   range based on the report velocity; the author does not configure overscan.
547:   A final range report at the end of a scroll returns to the small base margin.
548: - The engine reconciles window children by absolute index, or by an optional
549:   `key` extractor (`ForEach(items, key = { it.id })`); without a key, identity
550:   is the absolute index.
551: - Row-local component state (`by state(...)`) is scoped by the `ForEach` item key
552:   (or absolute index without a key) and survives window eviction: a re-created
553:   row rebinds to the same persisted state, and rows are independent.
554: - Paged sources: `ForEach(source: PagedDataSource<T>, itemExtent, placeholder)`
555:   loads pages on demand. Loaded rows render via the content; unloaded rows render
556:   the placeholder (a spacer by default) at `itemExtent`. The engine calls the
557:   source's prefetch for the initial and visible windows. `itemExtent` is
558:   required because the full list is not known up front. The source exposes
559:   `total`/`loading`/`error` signals; a page arrival re-renders only the lazy
560:   slot. SSR starts in the loading state; the live session loads pages.
561: - A full-snapshot/SSR emission carries the first window plus the full virtual
562:   extent; the client corrects the window after `META::ENVIRONMENT`.
563: - `LazyVGrid`/`LazyHGrid` use the same data-source window with a **row** or
564:   **column** unit: `ITEM_COUNT` is the row/column count, `ITEM_EXTENT` the row
565:   height/column width, and `FIRST_ITEM_INDEX` the first visible row/column. The
566:   emitted children are the cells of the visible units (row-major for VGrid,
567:   column-major for HGrid). The grid's `columns`/`rows` (or `GRID_TRACKS`)
568:   define the cells per unit. Rust: `LazyVGrid::children(vec![ForEach…])
569:   .with(|c| c.columns(n))` (and `LazyHGrid`/`rows`) consume the same window.
570: 
571: The window math, child placement, and visible-range derivation are specified in
572: [LAYOUT.md §Virtual extent](./LAYOUT.md#virtual-extent-lazy-containers). The
573: decision and rationale are in
574: [ADR-0014](../docs/decisions/0014-virtualized-lazy-stacks.md).

    <artifactId>pathland-server-core</artifactId>
    <packaging>jar</packaging>

    <name>Pathland Server Core</name>
    <description>
        Transport-agnostic Pathland server runtime: one Pathland app instance per session
        (SSR + live 16-byte opcode deltas + environment), the session registry, the
        Micrometer/OpenTelemetry telemetry adapters, and the shared WebSocket test
        harness, all used by the Spring Boot and Quarkus starters. Framework glue only
        lives in the starters; Redis lives in the opt-in pathland-state-redis module.
    </description>

    <dependencies>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.jetbrains.kotlin</groupId>
            <artifactId>kotlin-stdlib</artifactId>
            <version>${kotlin.version}</version>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
            <artifactId>pathland-core</artifactId>
            <version>${project.version}</version>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
            <artifactId>pathland-view-core</artifactId>
            <version>${project.version}</version>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
            <artifactId>pathland-render-html</artifactId>
            <version>${project.version}</version>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>io.micrometer</groupId>
            <artifactId>micrometer-core</artifactId>
        </dependency>
        <!-- The OTel API is optional: only needed when the host enables tracing. The
             starters add the OTel bridge/exporters that bring it in. -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>io.opentelemetry</groupId>
            <artifactId>opentelemetry-api</artifactId>
            <optional>true</optional>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.slf4j</groupId>
            <artifactId>slf4j-api</artifactId>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.junit.jupiter</groupId>
            <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
        <!-- A real OTel SDK (test scope) to assert the tracing decorator emits spans. -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>io.opentelemetry</groupId>
            <artifactId>opentelemetry-sdk</artifactId>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>io.opentelemetry</groupId>
            <artifactId>opentelemetry-sdk-testing</artifactId>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>
    <build>
        <plugins>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.jetbrains.kotlin</groupId>
                <artifactId>kotlin-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>${kotlin.version}</version>
                <executions>
                    <execution>
                        <id>test-compile</id>
                        <phase>process-test-sources</phase>

                    <languageVersion>2.4</languageVersion>
                    <apiVersion>2.4</apiVersion>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>
        </plugins>
    </build>
</project>

# ADR-0017: Latest-wins coalescing of lazy visible-range reports

**Status:** Proposed
**Recorded:** 2026-11-17
**Scope:** Lazy-window input handling, paged data sources, DOM client, server runtime
**Supersedes:** None (extends ADR-0014/ADR-0015)

## Context

A windowed lazy stack reports `EVENT::VISIBLE_RANGE` when its visible range
changes. A fast scrollbar drag can produce a report every animation frame across
a large distance. The engine applies each report to the window, and a paged data
source loads the pages covering every intermediate window. On a long list this
can load much or all of the dataset for a gesture the user never paused on,
competing with the final window's pages and delaying it.

Only the latest visible range in a continuous input burst is useful for
rendering and prefetch: intermediate ranges are already off-screen by the time
their pages arrive.

## Decision

Treat successive visible-range reports for the same target as a latest-wins
stream:

- The DOM client throttles scroll/resize-driven reports to at most one per
  ~100 ms and still sends a final report when the gesture ends. Reports after
  hydration, batch application, or connection open stay immediate.
- The server runtime MAY coalesce reports per `(session, target)` for a short
  interval (~50 ms) before dispatching to the session actor; non-range events
  dispatch immediately.
- A paged data source applies only the current requested window. A page result
  that arrives after the window moved is discarded: it is not cached, does not
  bump the version signal, and does not change loading/error state.

Exact behavior lives in [EVENTS.md §Visible range](../../spec/EVENTS.md#visible-range),
[LAYOUT.md §Virtual extent](../../spec/LAYOUT.md#virtual-extent-lazy-containers),
and [DSL.md §Virtualized lists](../../spec/DSL.md#virtualized-lists-lazyvstack--lazyhstack).
The renderer event surface and wire format are unchanged.

## Rationale

- Preserves ADR-0015's engine-owned prefetch: the final/current window still
  drives the bounded, directional margin.
- Bounds page I/O by the window the user settles on, not the path taken there.
- Renderer-agnostic: a client that reports every frame is corrected by the host,
  and the data source is safe regardless of report cadence.
- Keeps the protocol unchanged: `VISIBLE_RANGE` keeps its semantics; coalescing
  is quality-of-service at the engine/host boundary.

## Alternatives

- **Final-report-only** (suppress intermediate reports): rejected — the list
  would show placeholders during the drag and lose directional prefetch.
- **Data-source suppression only**: rejected — page I/O for intermediate windows
  still runs; only rendering is avoided.
- **Client throttle only**: rejected — other renderers/hosts would still
  dispatch every report.
- **Page cancellation/priority**: rejected for now — a larger I/O scheduler;
  latest-wins plus the current-window guard is simpler and sufficient.

## Consequences

- Intermediate page loads may be discarded; work is bounded by the final
  window's pages.
- Client cadence is a heuristic, not a protocol guarantee; the server and data
  source guards remain authoritative.
- The ~100 ms client and ~50 ms server intervals are implementation tuning, not
  author-configured overscan.
- Tests cover the client throttle, server coalescing, and stale-page discard.

- Lazy window: [LAYOUT.md §Virtual extent](../../spec/LAYOUT.md#virtual-extent-lazy-containers).
- Visible-range event: [EVENTS.md §Visible range](../../spec/EVENTS.md#visible-range).
- Authoring: [DSL.md §Virtualized lists](../../spec/DSL.md#virtualized-lists-lazyvstack--lazyhstack).
- Data sources: [docs/data-sources.md](../data-sources.md).
- Related decisions: [ADR-0014](0014-virtualized-lazy-stacks.md),
  [ADR-0015](0015-reactive-lazy-prefetch.md),
  [ADR-0016](0016-async-paged-data-sources.md).

Implemented the scrollbar-jump fix end to end.

- **Client:** scroll/resize `VISIBLE_RANGE` reports now throttle to ~100 ms with a trailing + `scrollend` final report (`lib/typescript/src/lazy-throttle.ts`, `index.ts`).
- **Server:** `PathlandRegistry` coalesces ranges latest-wins per `(session, target)` for ~50 ms; other events stay immediate (`VisibleRangeCoalescer`).
- **Source:** `PagedDataSource` discards page results outside the current window, without caching or touching `total`/`loading`/`error`.
- **ADR-0017:** added as **Proposed**, plus spec/docs/status updates.
- **Bonus bug found by the new end-to-end test:** `FrameCodec.encodeEvents` was dropping `VISIBLE_RANGE` first-index/count; fixed and covered.

## Plan: fast back-and-forth lazy-scroll regression tests

I inspected the changes. The likely weak spots are:
- `PagedDataSource` now **discards** any page result outside the immediate requested window; back-and-forth scrolling can repeatedly throw away pages and reload them.
- `LazyWindowTracker` returns an empty window when `ITEM_COUNT` is still 0, so a range that arrives before the count is known can snap the list back to the top.
- The server coalescer adds a delay; the tests need to prove the **final settled window** actually renders after a burst.

These existing tests don’t exercise page completions interleaved with rapid window changes, or the client’s post-batch range reports.

### 1. Engine/data-source test (`pathland-view-core`)
New `PagedFastScrollTest`:
- Large list: 1,000 rows, e.g. 20 rows/page, controlled `PagedDataSource.ofAsync` futures.
- Mount `LazyVStack` + `ForEach(source, itemExtent, placeholder)` with `Text("row-$i")`.
- Drive the lazy node’s `VisibleRangeInput` from `RenderResult.visibleRanges()`: `800 → 100 → 650 → 250 → 500 → 50 → 900 → 300`, completing pages out of order between ranges.
- After each settle, call `emitter.renderFull()` and assert:
  - `ITEM_COUNT` stays 1000.
  - `FIRST_ITEM_INDEX` matches the settled window.
  - the full frame contains the settled window’s row labels (e.g. `row-300`).
  - no stale window rows remain and the frame is never empty.
- Add a case where a range arrives **before** page 0/total is known; assert the list honors that range once the count arrives rather than resetting to the top.
- Add a case where an old-window page completes **after** the final range; assert it cannot overwrite the settled rows.

### 2. Registry/server test (`pathland-server-core`)
New `FastScrollRegistryTest`:
- Real `PathlandRegistry` + paged lazy app + recording connection.
- Send the back-and-forth ranges as **separate batches** (as the DOM client does), not one batch, with short gaps.
- After settling, request `registry.resync("ui")`, decode the full frame, and assert the final `SET_TEXT` rows, `FIRST_ITEM_INDEX`, and total. Also assert non-range events still dispatch immediately.
- This covers coalescer → session → source → final rendered frame.

### 3. Client throttle test (`lib/typescript`)
Extend `lazy-throttle.test.ts`:
- Burst scrolls back and forth; assert bounded emission, a trailing report, and that the **last** emitted range is the final position.
- Add a DOM-level test around `refreshLazyWindows` with mocked scroller geometry: a burst should produce the final `VISIBLE_RANGE`, and applying a simulated final-window frame should leave the expected rows/padding/ARIA in place.

### 4. Real-browser test (optional, opt-in)
New `e2e/library-fast-scroll.spec.ts`:
- Skip unless `PATHLAND_URL` points at a running Quarkus/Spring demo.
- Wait for the library, rapidly drive the scroll container back and forth, settle, and assert visible rows have the expected `aria-posinset`/text, the list is non-empty, and the position did not jump to the top.
- I’ll run this against the demo during verification.

### 5. Fix based on failures
The tests will determine the smallest fix. Likely candidates:
- Preserve the pending visible range until `ITEM_COUNT` is known (no top-snap).
- If back-and-forth blanking/reloading is caused by the **discard** policy, switch to caching stale pages but not rendering/versioning them for the current window. This reverses the earlier “discard” choice, so I’ll confirm before changing it.
- Only if the tests show it, tune or repair the server coalescing/throttle so the final range is never dropped.

### Questions
1. What exactly does “broken” look like: blank rows, wrong rows, jump to top, list never settles, or a crash?
2. If the tests show that discarding stale pages causes the breakage, may I switch to **cache-without-render** for stale pages?
3. Is an opt-in Playwright demo test acceptable, or do you want CI-only JVM/TS tests?
1: black rows 2: yes 3: you decide
1: black rows 2: yes 3: you decide, but prefer jvm/ts tests

## Final plan: fix black/blank rows during fast back-and-forth scrolling

Confirmed decisions:
- Symptom: rows render black/empty during fast scrolling.
- Stale pages: **cache without rendering** (replaces the earlier “discard” policy).
- Tests: JVM + TypeScript only; no Playwright.

### Root cause hypothesis
The discard guard is the likely trigger. With back-and-forth ranges, each window change throws away page results that are in flight, so rows remain as dark skeletons/blank and the source re-requests pages repeatedly. A range that arrives before `ITEM_COUNT` is known can also reset the window to the top. I’ll encode both as failing tests before changing behavior.

### 1. Regression tests (JVM, primary)
**`pathland-view-core` — new `PagedFastScrollTest`**
- 1,000 rows, 20/page, controlled async page completions.
- Mount `LazyVStack` + `ForEach(source, itemExtent, placeholder)` with `Text("row-$i")`.
- Drive `VisibleRangeInput` back and forth: `800 → 100 → 650 → 250 → 500 → 50 → 900 → 300`, completing pages out of order.
- After settling, `emitter.renderFull()` and assert:
  - `ITEM_COUNT` stays 1000; `FIRST_ITEM_INDEX` is the settled window.
  - the settled rows’ text is present (not empty/skeleton), and stale window rows are absent.
  - the frame is never empty/blank.
- Add “range before total”: hold page 0, send range 700, release page 0; assert the window settles around 700, not the top.
- Add “old page completes late”: assert it is cached but cannot render in the new window; moving back renders it **without a new loader call**.

**`pathland-server-core` — extend `VisibleRangeRegistryTest`**
- Send back-and-forth ranges as **separate batches**, not one batch.
- After settling, `registry.resync("ui")` and assert the full snapshot contains the settled rows/`FIRST_ITEM_INDEX`, not placeholders.
- Keep the coalescer/latest-wins assertions and non-range-immediate behavior.

### 2. Implementation changes
**`PagedDataSource`**
- Cache every successful page result (bounded LRU stays).
- Update `total`/`hasMore` from any completed page.
- Bump `version` only when the page intersects the current window, so stale pages are cached but never cause stale rows to render.
- Ignore stale-page failures (current behavior); keep `inFlight` cleanup.
- Update `PagedDataSourceTest`: stale success is cached but not rendered; stale failure still does not set `error`.

**`LazyWindowTracker` / `LazyStackView`**
- Remember the latest requested visible range while `ITEM_COUNT` is unknown.
- When the count becomes known, apply that range instead of falling back to the initial top window.
- Clear the pending range once applied.

**TS**
- Extend `lazy-throttle.test.ts`: rapid back-and-forth burst emits bounded reports and the **final** range is the latest position.
- Add a lightweight `refreshLazyWindows` test with mocked scroller geometry: the client emits the final `VISIBLE_RANGE`, and a simulated settled window keeps the correct row count/ARIA (no empty range).
- No client code change unless this test exposes a reporting bug.

### 3. Contingency
If the registry test still shows blank final rows after caching, adjust only the coalescer behavior (shorter interval or leading+trailing flush). The ADR-0017/coalescer design stays otherwise.

### 4. Documentation/status
Update ADR-0017, `spec/DSL.md`, `docs/data-sources.md`, and the affected `status.md` files from “discard” to “cache without rendering”, and record the new regression tests.

### 5. Verification
- `mvn -P jvm-only test`
- `npm --prefix lib/typescript test` + typecheck
- `cargo test` (unchanged, sanity)
- `scripts/check-references.py`, `git diff --check`

The main focus is to reproduce the issue with tests and then fix it

## Test-first plan: reproduce black/blank rows, then fix

I’ll treat “black rows” as empty/placeholder rows showing through during fast scroll. The protocol doesn’t carry a “black” style; the tests will assert the row **content** (text vs placeholder), the window index, and the child count.

### Phase 1 — Add failing reproductions (no production changes)

**A. `PagedFastScrollTest` (`pathland-view-core`) — primary reproduction**

Use a controlled `PagedDataSource.ofAsync` with per-call `CompletableFuture`s, 50-row pages, 1,000 rows, and a placeholder that renders `placeholder-$i`.

Test 1: `returningToAPreviouslyRequestedWindowUsesTheCachedPage`
1. Mount the lazy list; complete page 0 so `ITEM_COUNT = 1000`.
2. Move to window `100..119`; **do not** complete page 2 yet.
3. Move to window `500..519`; complete page 2 while the window is elsewhere.
4. Move back to `100..119`; complete nothing.
5. Assert the full frame (`emitter.renderFull()`) contains `row-100` / `row-119`, not `placeholder-100`.
6. Assert the loader was called **once** for offset 100.

Expected current failure: the page was discarded, so the second call starts another load and the frame contains placeholders/black rows.

Test 2: `rangeBeforeTheCountDoesNotSnapToTheTop`
1. Mount; leave page 0 incomplete.
2. Send `VISIBLE_RANGE(700, 20)`.
3. Complete page 0 with `total = 1000`.
4. Complete the page requested for 700.
5. Assert `FIRST_ITEM_INDEX` is near 700 and the frame contains `row-700`.

Expected current failure: the tracker saw `total = 0`, discarded the range, reset to the initial top window, and the viewport ends up over an empty/placeholder region.

Test 3: `backAndForthNeverLeavesTheSettledWindowBlank`
- Drive `800 → 100 → 650 → 250 → 500` with out-of-order page completions.
- After settling, assert `ITEM_COUNT = 1000`, the settled rows are present, stale rows are absent, and the frame contains no placeholder-only window.

Update `PagedDataSourceTest`: the stale-page test now expects the page to be **cached but not rendered**, not `null`.

**B. Registry integration (`pathland-server-core`)**
Extend `VisibleRangeRegistryTest` with the same fast back-and-forth sequence, sending **separate batches**:
- Control page futures through the app’s source.
- After returning to a previously requested window, call `registry.resync("ui")` and assert the snapshot contains the settled row text without completing a second load.
- This reproduces the black-row behavior through coalescer → session → source.

**C. TypeScript**
- Extend `lazy-throttle.test.ts`: back-and-forth burst emits bounded reports and the final range is the latest position.
- Add a `refreshLazyWindows` test with mocked scroller geometry: rapid back-and-forth reports the correct final range and leaves the correct window/ARIA state, with no empty range.

### Phase 2 — Minimal fix

1. **`PagedDataSource`: cache without rendering**
   - Cache every successful page (bounded LRU remains).
   - Update `total`/`hasMore` from any completed page.
   - Bump `version` only when the page intersects the current window; stale pages are cached but never add rows to the current window.
   - Keep ignoring stale failures; keep `inFlight` cleanup.
   - Protect current-window pages from LRU eviction if needed.

2. **`LazyWindowTracker` / `LazyStackView`: preserve a pre-count range**
   - Remember the latest requested `(first, count)` while `data.count() == 0`.
   - When the count becomes known, compute and apply that window instead of `initialWindow` at the top.
   - Clear the pending range once applied.

3. **Server coalescer**
   - No change unless the registry reproduction shows the final range is dropped or applied too late; then use a shorter interval or leading+trailing flush.

- Run the new tests against the old code first and record the failures.
- Apply the fix; rerun the new tests.
- Run `mvn -P jvm-only test`, TS tests + typecheck, `cargo test`, `scripts/check-references.py`, `git diff --check`.

Reproduced and fixed the black/blank-row regression.

**Reproduction (failed before the fix):**
- `PagedFastScrollTest.returningToAPreviouslyRequestedWindowUsesTheCachedPage` returned placeholder rows (`placeholder-100…`) and fetched page 2 twice.
- `PagedFastScrollTest.aRangeBeforeTheCountDoesNotSnapTheListBackToTheTop` reported `FIRST_ITEM_INDEX=0` after a range sent before the count arrived.
- Added a registry-level assertion that the resync snapshot renders the settled rows, plus TS back-and-forth range/throttle tests.

**Fix:**
- `PagedDataSource` now caches every completed page (bounded), but only publishes a render version when the page intersects the current window; stale failures are ignored.
- `LazyStackView`/`LazyGridWindowView` preserve a visible range received before `ITEM_COUNT` is known and apply it when the count arrives instead of resetting to the top.
- Updated the ADR/spec/docs/status wording from “discard” to “cache without rendering”.

**Verification:** all 3 new fast-scroll tests pass; full `mvn -P jvm-only test`, TS 302 tests + typecheck, Rust tests + engine traces, references, and `git diff --check` all pass. No commit.

quarkus.http.port=8080
quarkus.http.host=0.0.0.0
quarkus.log.category."dev.pathland".level=INFO

# --- HSTS (whole-origin, app-owned) --------------------------------------------
# The extension deliberately does not default HSTS: it pins the entire origin
# (all paths/ports, and subdomains with includeSubDomains) in the browser. This
# demo is served only over HTTPS behind Render's TLS terminator, so opt in here.
# Drop includeSubDomains if any subdomain may remain on plain HTTP; only add
# preload if the domain is intentionally submitted to the HSTS preload list.
quarkus.http.header."Strict-Transport-Security".value=max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains

# --- Same-server proxy demo (spec/PROXY.md) ------------------------------------
# The music player at / embeds the small ad app mounted at /ad (this same server)
# as a sponsored slot in its Now Playing pane, via a ProxyView. This is the origin
# app's base URL the player proxies; point it at another host/port to proxy a
# remote app instead.
pathland.demo.ad-url=http://localhost:8080/ad

# --- Per-window id on the first request (issue #155) ---------------------------
# Opt the DOM client into the service worker that attaches the per-window id to
# top-level navigations, so the SSR renders the right persisted-state scope on the
# FIRST paint (instead of defaults that the live connection then corrects). The id
# never appears in the URL. Off by default; the worker is served at /_pathland/sw.js
# with Service-Worker-Allowed: / (root scope) and no-cache.
pathland.service-worker=true

# The DOM client bundle ships in the Quarkus extension jar (`META-INF/resources`)
# and is served by Quarkus's static handler. The demo's media/icons are served
# from a disk extraction via DemoAssetsRoute, which sends its own caching headers.
quarkus.http.static-resources.max-age=168h

# Pathland SSR debug comments: when true, every rendered HTML node is prefixed
# with a comment naming its component type and the modifiers applied, e.g.
#   <!-- #1 VStack: spacing=4, alignment=Fill -->
# Debugging aid — opt-in; the live /ws deltas are unaffected.
# pathland.debug-html=true

# --- Observability (issue #62) -------------------------------------------------
# Structured (JSON) console logging — the production-shaped reference app default.
quarkus.log.console.json.enabled=true
# Metrics: Micrometer counters/timers at pathland.* are exposed at /q/metrics
# (Prometheus); health at /q/health (smallrye-health). See pathland-server-core.
#
# OpenTelemetry spans per frame send / event batch are OPT-IN. The starter wires the
# tracing decorator automatically when a Tracer is available, so to enable them just
# add the extension and point it at a collector:
#   <dependency>io.quarkus:quarkus-opentelemetry</dependency>
#   quarkus.otel.exporter.otlp.traces.endpoint=http://localhost:4317
# (the extension is intentionally NOT a dependency here, so local dev is quiet).

# --- SEO document head (issue #45) --------------------------------------------
# Canonical/OG/Twitter/JSON-LD are emitted by default; the app can refine them
# per route via PathlandApp.pageMetadata(...).

/**
 * The music player demo: a track library, now-playing sidebar with album art,
 * and a bottom player bar. Asserts the rendered tree and that interactions drive
 * the persisted player state.
 */
class MusicPlayerViewTest {

    private data class Mounted(
        val result: RenderResult,
        val sink: FrameOpcodeSink,
        val store: StateStore,
    )

    private class MultiFrameSink : FrameOpcodeSink() {
        val frames = mutableListOf<ProtocolFrame>()

        override fun endFrame() {
            super.endFrame()
            frames.add(frame())
        }
    }

    private fun mount(snapshot: Boolean = false): Mounted {
        val store = InMemoryStateStore()
        val state = PersistentState(store, "session-1")
        val sink = FrameOpcodeSink()
        val emitter = Emitter(sink)
        if (snapshot) emitter.snapshotEmission(true)
        val result = emitter.mount(MusicPlayerView.make(), Environment(state))
        return Mounted(result, sink, store)
    }

    private fun mountAd(): Mounted {
        val store = InMemoryStateStore()
        val sink = FrameOpcodeSink()
        val emitter = Emitter(sink)
        emitter.snapshotEmission(true)
        val result = emitter.mount(
            MusicPlayerView.make("http://localhost:8080/ad"),
            Environment(PersistentState(store, "session-1")),
        )
        return Mounted(result, sink, store)
    }

    @Test
    fun libraryRendersTracksAndAlbumArt() {
        val frame = mount().sink.frame()

        assertTrue(anySetText(frame, "Building on Solid Ground"))
        assertTrue(anySetText(frame, "Rendered Free"))
        assertTrue(anySetText(frame, "The Pathland Dream"))
        assertTrue(anySetText(frame, "The Foundation"))
        assertFalse(anySetText(frame, "Now Playing"))
        assertTrue(anySetText(frame, "Library"))
        assertTrue(countCreate(frame, Components.IMAGE) >= 3)
        assertTrue(anySetPropertyString(frame, Properties.IMAGE_SOURCE, COVER))
        assertEquals(1, countCreate(frame, Components.VIEW_THAT_FITS))
        assertEquals(1, countCreate(frame, Components.MEDIA_CONTROLLER))
    }

    @Test
    fun libraryUsesAWindowedList() {
        val frame = mount().sink.frame()

        assertEquals(1, countCreate(frame, Components.LAZY_VSTACK))
        assertTrue(anySetProperty(frame, Properties.ITEM_COUNT, 1000))
        assertTrue(anySetProperty(frame, Properties.ITEM_EXTENT, LIBRARY_ROW_HEIGHT))
        assertTrue(anySetProperty(frame, Properties.FIRST_ITEM_INDEX, 0))
        // Only the initial window (20 + overscan 2) is emitted, not 1000 rows.
        assertTrue(countCreate(frame, Components.IMAGE) in 1..40)
    }

    @Test
    fun fitShowsTheSidebarWhenTheParentIsWideEnough() {
        val mounted = mount()
        val slotId = slotIdByMaxThreshold(mounted.sink.frame(), 1024f)
        assertFalse(anySetText(mounted.sink.frame(), "Now Playing"))

        mounted.result.fitInputs()[slotId]!!.accept(2)
        val wide = mounted.sink.frame()

        assertTrue(anySetText(wide, "Now Playing"))
        assertTrue(anySetText(wide, "Up Next"))
        assertEquals(0, countCreate(wide, Components.MEDIA_CONTROLLER))
        assertEquals(0, countCreate(wide, Components.VIEW_THAT_FITS))
    }

    @Test
    fun playerBarRendersTransportAndSliders() {
        val mounted = mount()
        val frame = mounted.sink.frame()

        // The narrow player bar has the play/pause transport button; the
        // library rows are tappable HStacks, not buttons.
        assertTrue(countCreate(frame, Components.BUTTON) >= 1)
        assertEquals(1, countCreate(frame, Components.SLIDER))
        assertTrue(anySlider(frame, 0f, 100f))
        assertTrue(anySetText(frame, "|"))
        assertTrue(anySetPropertyString(
            frame,
            Properties.MEDIA_SOURCE,
            "/_pathland/assets/audio/track1.mp3",
        ))
        assertTrue(anySetProperty(frame, Properties.PLAYBACK_STATE, 0))
        assertTrue(anySetProperty(frame, Properties.MEDIA_POSITION, 0f))

        val rootSlot = slotIdByMaxThreshold(frame, 1024f)
        mounted.result.fitInputs()[rootSlot]!!.accept(1)
        val medium = mounted.sink.frame()
        assertTrue(anySlider(medium, 0f, 1f))
        assertTrue(anySliderValue(medium, 0.7f))

        mounted.result.fitInputs()[rootSlot]!!.accept(2)
        val withSidebar = mounted.sink.frame()
        assertTrue(anySetText(withSidebar, "Now Playing"))
        assertTrue(anySetText(withSidebar, "Up Next"))
    }

    @Test
    fun snapshotEmissionCarriesEveryCandidate() {
        val mounted = mount(snapshot = true)
        val frame = mounted.sink.frame()

        assertTrue(anySetText(frame, "Library"))
        assertTrue(anySetText(frame, "Now Playing"))

content.text:
## Root cause found in the Quarkus demo

I inspected the running demo in a headless browser. The bug is in the DOM client’s virtual-padding calculation, not in the engine or page cache:

- Downward works: `paddingTop` grows correctly (`first 0 → 44 → 138`, padding `0 → 2816 → 8832`).
- Upward fails: `data-pathland-first-item-index` falls (`138 → 84 → 37 → 0`), but `paddingTop` stays at `8832px`.
- Result: rows remain positioned thousands of pixels below the viewport; the visible area is just the old top padding — blank entries.

Cause: `lazyBase()` in `lib/typescript/src/apply.ts` re-derives the app’s base padding as `currentPadding - newExtra` and then adds `newExtra` back. That is only correct while the leading grows. When the window moves up and the leading shrinks, it keeps the old larger padding. Live-created lazy elements have no `data-pathland-base-padding-*` attributes, so this fallback is used. SSR elements have the attributes and do not show the bug.

## Plan

### 1. Reproduce with tests (fail first)
**TS regression test (`apply.test.ts` or new `lazy-window.test.ts`)**
- Create a live-style lazy element: count 1000, extent 64, no base-padding attrs.
- Call `refreshLazyWindows` with `first = 0`, then `138`, then `84`, then `0`.
- Assert:
  - `paddingTop` is `first * 64` (or base + leading), including when `first` decreases.
  - `paddingBottom` updates correctly in both directions.
  - `data-pathland-base-padding-*` is established once and remains stable.
  - The upward `VISIBLE_RANGE` is still reported correctly.
- Add a scroller/geometry case: window first 138, viewport at row 84; after refresh, assert the rows for 84 are within the scroller viewport (not below it).

**Optional live-browser test**
- Add an opt-in `e2e/library-scroll.spec.ts` gated on `PATHLAND_URL`: scroll down, then up, and assert a visible row’s `aria-posinset` and bounding rect stay inside the scroller. This exactly covers the Quarkus path.

### 2. Fix the client padding
In `lib/typescript/src/apply.ts`:
- Stop deriving base padding from the current computed padding.
- Use, in order:
  1. the SSR-provided `data-pathland-base-padding-*` value, or
  2. a stable per-element base recorded on the first refresh (and write it back to `data-pathland-base-padding-*` for live-created elements).
- Always compute `paddingTop = baseTop + leading` and `paddingBottom = baseBottom + trailing`, so both can shrink and grow.
- Keep the SSR path unchanged.

No server/engine changes are needed; the JVM cache and pending-range tests already pass.

### 3. Rebuild and verify the Quarkus demo
The demo serves the bundled DOM client from the Quarkus extension:
1. `npm --prefix lib/typescript run build:all` (new content-hashed bundle).
2. `mvn -q -DskipTests install` in `lib/java` so the Quarkus demo uses the new extension/server jars.
3. Restart `quarkus:dev`; hard-reload / clear the service worker cache (the demo enables `pathland.service-worker=true`).
4. Re-run the browser probe: scroll down to ~9000px, then back up to ~3000/1000/0; rows must remain in the viewport and `paddingTop` must fall with `FIRST_ITEM_INDEX`.

### 4. Regression checks
- TS tests + typecheck.
- Full JVM suite.
- Rust tests/engine traces unchanged.
- `scripts/check-references.py`, `git diff --check`.

No protocol or spec change is required; this is a renderer padding bug.

  support variable item extents (`data-pathland-item-extents` /

  mapping. Lazy grids use the same window with `data-pathland-lazy-tracks` and
  grid a11y (`role=grid`/`gridcell`, row/column indices). Scroll/resize-driven
  reports are throttled to one per ~100 ms with a trailing report; a `scrollend`
  listener plus a 150 ms debounce forces a final `VISIBLE_RANGE` report so the
  engine can release prefetched rows (ADR-0015/ADR-0017). Batch application,
  hydration, and reconnect reports stay immediate.

todos.content: Add failing TS regression test for shrinking virtual padding
Fix lazy base-padding calculation for upward windows
Run TS tests + typecheck; rebuild DOM bundle
Verify against running Quarkus demo (down then up)
Run full JVM/Rust/reference checks and update status

content.text:
Fixed the upward blanking in the Quarkus demo.

**Root cause:** `lazyBase()` derived base padding from the *current* virtual padding, so when scrolling up and the leading shrank, the padding kept its larger old value. Rows stayed below the viewport.

**Changes:**
- Added a regression test that fails on the old code: `shrinks the virtual padding when the window moves back up`.
- `lazyBase()` now records a stable per-element base padding on first refresh (SSR `data-pathland-base-padding-*` still wins), so leading/trailing can both shrink and grow.
- Rebuilt the DOM bundle (`dom-renderer-05c1a3b75a6f.js`) and installed the JVM modules.

**Verified:** fresh Quarkus demo, scrolling down `0 → 3000 → 9000` and back up `6000 → 3000 → 1000 → 0`; padding now tracks `FIRST_ITEM_INDEX` and rows remain visible. TS 303 tests, typecheck, full JVM suite, references, and diff checks pass.

Restart your running Quarkus demo on `:8080` and hard-reload/clear the service worker so it picks up the new content-hashed bundle. Not committed.
